title: I couldn’t find a simple free tool for splitting and previewing sprite sheets, so I built one
author: Feisty-Ad-1805
selftext:
I’ve been working on a small side-scrolling game as a personal project, mostly just for fun and to learn more about game development.

One of the things I struggled with was working with sprite sheets. I needed a simple way to split them into individual frames, preview the animation, and prepare the sprites for my game.

I started looking for tools that could help, but many of the ones I found were either paid, more complicated than I needed, or didn’t have everything I wanted in one place.

Since I’m still learning game development, I really just wanted something simple, fast, and free.

So… I decided to build it myself. 😄

I created SplitterPNG, a free web tool that lets you:

Split sprite sheets and PNG images into individual frames

Preview and animate sprites directly in the browser

Export animations as GIFs

Remove image backgrounds

Download the resulting frames

I originally built it just to solve my own problem, and I’ve actually been using it while creating sprites for my game. It ended up being much more useful than I expected, so I decided to put it online for anyone to use for free.

Hopefully it can help other indie developers, artists, or people who are just getting started with game development like me.

I’d also genuinely appreciate feedback. If there’s something that would make it more useful for your sprite workflow, let me know — I’m still actively improving it.

SplitterPNG: splitterpng.vercel.app
